title: Which Aluminum Suppliers Include Mill Certs, and Which Gate Them
summary: OnlineMetals includes a free MTR by checkbox. McMaster offers traceability certificates. Yarde puts certs behind a portal login. Four others publish nothing. A survey of who actually gives you the paperwork.
body_markdown:
### Do aluminum suppliers charge for mill certs?


It varies and most do not publish it. OnlineMetals.com provides a free printed mill test report on qualifying material when you check the box at checkout. NOX METALS includes mill certs with heat numbers and lot traceability on every order at no additional cost. Several suppliers publish nothing, so ask before ordering.


### What is the difference between a mill cert and an MTR?


They are usually the same document under different names: a mill test report or mill certification issued by the producing mill documenting chemistry and mechanical properties for a specific heat. What matters more is whether it also states melt source, which is required for a DFARS flow-down, and whether it references your heat number.


### Is a certificate of conformance the same as a mill cert?


No. A certificate of conformance is the supplier asserting the material meets your order. A mill cert is the producing mill's test data for your specific heat. On regulated work you generally need the mill cert, and a certificate of conformance alone is frequently rejected.


### Does ISO 9001 certification mean I get mill certs?


No. ISO 9001:2015 certifies the supplier's quality management system, not your material. A supplier can be ISO certified and still ship you undocumented metal. Ask specifically what material certification arrives with the order.


### How long should a supplier keep my mill certs?


Long enough to cover your audit and contract retention requirements, which on defense and aerospace work often runs years past delivery. Ask for the retention period and whether they can reissue, and keep your own copy regardless. Do not rely on a supplier portal as your only archive.
